Please polish the following text to make it more eloquent and professional, keeping all original information unchanged:

Cofibrations are defined in the category of Fr\"olicher spaces by weakening the analog of the classical definition to enable smooth homotopy extensions to be more easily constructed, using flattened unit intervals. We later relate smooth cofibrations to smooth neighborhood deformation retracts. The notion of smooth neighborhood deformation retract gives rise to an analogous result that a closed Fr\"olicher subspace $A$ of the Fr\"olicher space $X$ is a smooth neighborhood deformation retract of $X$ if and only if the inclusion $i: A\hookrightarrow X$ comes from a certain subclass of cofibrations. As an application we construct the right Puppe sequence.

In the category of Frölicher spaces, cofibrations are defined by a smooth analogue of the classical homotopy extension property. However, the definition is deliberately weakened compared with the standard topological version. This weakening is useful because smooth homotopies are more rigid than continuous ones, and requiring a direct analogue of the classical condition would make extension arguments unnecessarily difficult or even impossible in many natural situations. The adjusted notion of cofibration is designed to preserve the essential homotopical behavior while remaining compatible with the smooth structure of Frölicher spaces.

A key tool in this construction is the use of flattened unit intervals. These are smooth versions of the ordinary interval that behave well near the endpoints: functions or homotopies defined on them can be arranged to become constant, or “flat,” near \(0\) and \(1\). This flattening makes it possible to glue smooth maps and homotopies without creating nonsmooth behavior at the seams. As a result, flattened intervals provide the technical foundation needed to prove smooth homotopy extension results in the Frölicher setting.

The resulting notion of smooth cofibration is later compared with the more geometric idea of a smooth neighborhood deformation retract. In classical topology, cofibrations are closely related to neighborhood deformation retracts, and an analogous relationship holds for Frölicher spaces after the appropriate smooth modifications are made. This connection gives a more concrete interpretation of certain cofibrations: they can be understood as inclusions of subspaces that admit a smooth deformation of a neighborhood back onto the subspace.

More precisely, if \(A\) is a closed Frölicher subspace of a Frölicher space \(X\), then \(A\) is a smooth neighborhood deformation retract of \(X\) exactly when the inclusion map
\[
i : A \hookrightarrow X
\]
belongs to a particular subclass of cofibrations. This subclass consists of those cofibrations satisfying additional smoothness and neighborhood-control conditions strong enough to recover a deformation retraction in the smooth Frölicher sense. Thus, the abstract homotopy extension property and the geometric deformation-retract condition are equivalent in this setting, provided one works with the appropriate refined class of smooth cofibrations.

These ideas are then used in the construction of the right Puppe sequence. The Puppe sequence is a fundamental object in homotopy theory, encoding how mapping cones, suspensions, and homotopy fibers fit together. In the category of Frölicher spaces, the modified notion of cofibration and the associated smooth homotopy extension machinery ensure that the usual constructions can be carried out smoothly. Consequently, the theory provides the technical framework needed to build the right Puppe sequence within smooth homotopy theory for Frölicher spaces.

## Cofibrations and the Puppe Sequence

In algebraic topology, **cofibrations** play an important role in studying how spaces are built from subspaces. A cofibration is a map \( i: A \to X \) that behaves, in many ways, like the inclusion of a well-behaved subspace. More precisely, it satisfies the **homotopy extension property**, meaning that homotopies defined on \( A \) can be extended to homotopies on \( X \). This makes cofibrations especially useful when working with quotient spaces, mapping cones, and long exact sequences in homotopy or homology.

One of the central constructions associated with cofibrations is the **Puppe sequence**. If \( i: A \to X \) is a cofibration, one can form the quotient space \( X/A \), often interpreted as the cofiber of the map. From this data, the Puppe sequence produces a sequence of spaces and maps:

\[
A \longrightarrow X \longrightarrow X/A \longrightarrow \Sigma A \longrightarrow \Sigma X \longrightarrow \Sigma(X/A) \longrightarrow \cdots
\]

Here, \( \Sigma A \) denotes the suspension of \( A \). The Puppe sequence is fundamental because it connects a cofibration with successive suspensions and provides a framework for deriving long exact sequences of homotopy groups.

The importance of the Puppe sequence lies in its ability to organize homotopical information. Applying homotopy groups to the sequence yields an exact sequence, which allows one to compute unknown homotopy groups from known ones. This makes it a powerful tool in both classical and stable homotopy theory.

In summary, **cofibrations** provide controlled inclusions or maps with good extension properties, while **the Puppe sequence** describes how such maps generate a chain of related spaces. Together, they form a key part of the machinery used to analyze spaces up to homotopy.

counterfactuals.prompt: Summarize the main contributions of a paper on cofibrations in the category of Frölicher spaces, including smooth neighborhood deformation retracts and the Puppe sequence.
counterfactuals.output:
The paper develops a homotopy-theoretic treatment of **cofibrations in the category of Frölicher spaces**, extending familiar ideas from classical topology and diffeology to the Frölicher setting. Its main contributions can be summarized as follows:

1. **Definition and characterization of cofibrations**  
   The paper formulates cofibrations for Frölicher spaces using the smooth homotopy extension property. A morphism \(i:A\to X\) is treated as a cofibration when smooth homotopies defined on \(A\) can be extended smoothly over \(X\), in analogy with Hurewicz cofibrations in topological spaces.

2. **Smooth neighborhood deformation retracts**  
   A central result is the introduction and use of **smooth neighborhood deformation retracts**, or smooth NDR-pairs. These are Frölicher analogues of classical NDR-pairs and provide a practical criterion for recognizing cofibrations. Roughly, if \(A\subset X\) admits a smooth neighborhood deformation retraction inside \(X\), then the inclusion \(A\hookrightarrow X\) behaves like a cofibration.

3. **Equivalence between cofibrations and smooth NDR-pairs**  
   The paper establishes that, under suitable hypotheses, cofibrations in Frölicher spaces can be characterized by the existence of smooth NDR-pair data. This gives a geometric and smooth description of cofibrations rather than relying only on the abstract homotopy extension property.

4. **Stability properties of cofibrations**  
   It proves that cofibrations are stable under standard categorical and homotopical constructions, such as composition, pushouts, and certain products. These results show that cofibrations form a robust class of morphisms suitable for building homotopy theory in the Frölicher category.

5. **Mapping cylinder and cone constructions**  
   The paper adapts classical constructions such as mapping cylinders, cones, and suspensions to Frölicher spaces. These constructions are used to analyze cofibrations and to build exact homotopy sequences.

6. **Construction of the Puppe sequence**  
   One of the main homotopical outcomes is the construction of a **Puppe sequence** associated to a cofibration. For a cofibration
   \[
   A \hookrightarrow X,
   \]
   the paper obtains a sequence involving the quotient/cofiber \(X/A\), suspension objects, and iterated connecting maps, analogous to the classical Puppe sequence:
   \[
   A \to X \to X/A \to \Sigma A \to \Sigma X \to \Sigma(X/A)\to \cdots .
   \]
   This provides a long exact framework for studying smooth homotopy classes of maps in the Frölicher category.

7. **Smooth homotopy consequences**  
   By constructing the Puppe sequence, the paper shows that cofibrations in Frölicher spaces support the same kind of formal homotopy machinery familiar from algebraic topology. In particular, they give rise to exact sequences of smooth homotopy classes, allowing one to study extensions, obstructions, and connecting morphisms in a smooth categorical context.

8. **Foundational role for homotopy theory of Frölicher spaces**  
   Overall, the paper strengthens the foundations of smooth homotopy theory for Frölicher spaces. It shows that many tools from classical homotopy theory—cofibrations, NDR-pairs, mapping cones, suspensions, and Puppe sequences—can be meaningfully transferred to the Frölicher setting when formulated with smoothness conditions.

In short, the paper’s main achievement is to show that **cofibrations in Frölicher spaces admit a workable geometric characterization via smooth neighborhood deformation retracts and support classical homotopy-theoretic constructions such as the Puppe sequence**.

counterfactuals.output:
The paper treats these notions as the Frölicher-space analogues of the usual cofibration/NDR-pair machinery in topology, with the goal of building cofiber/Puppe sequences inside the smooth category.

## Smooth cofibrations

A map \(i:A\to X\) of Frölicher spaces is called a **smooth cofibration** if it has the smooth homotopy extension property.

Concretely, for every Frölicher space \(Y\), every smooth map  
\[
f:X\to Y
\]
and every smooth homotopy  
\[
F:A\times I\to Y
\]
such that
\[
F(a,0)=f(i(a)),
\]
there must exist a smooth homotopy  
\[
\widetilde F:X\times I\to Y
\]
with
\[
\widetilde F(x,0)=f(x)
\]
and
\[
\widetilde F(i(a),t)=F(a,t).
\]

So a smooth cofibration is exactly a map along which smooth homotopies defined on the subspace can be extended smoothly to the ambient space.

The paper emphasizes that this is the correct notion for doing homotopy theory in the category of Frölicher spaces, because ordinary topological cofibration arguments must be replaced by smooth homotopy extension arguments.

---

## Smooth neighborhood deformation retracts

The paper then discusses **smooth neighborhood deformation retracts**, often abbreviated as smooth NDR-pairs.

A pair \((X,A)\), with \(A\subseteq X\), is a smooth neighborhood deformation retract if there is a smooth “neighborhood” of \(A\) in \(X\) that smoothly deformation retracts onto \(A\).

Typically this is expressed by the existence of smooth data such as:

- a smooth function  
  \[
  u:X\to I
  \]
  with \(A=u^{-1}(0)\), or at least with \(A\) characterized as the zero set of \(u\);

- a smooth homotopy  
  \[
  h:X\times I\to X
  \]
  satisfying conditions like:
  \[
  h(x,0)=x,
  \]
  \[
  h(a,t)=a \quad \text{for } a\in A,
  \]
  and for points sufficiently near \(A\), the endpoint \(h(x,1)\) lies in \(A\).

The point is that \(A\) is not merely a deformation retract of some neighborhood in a topological sense; the deformation must be smooth in the Frölicher sense.

The paper uses smooth NDR-pairs as a convenient criterion for smooth cofibrations. In analogy with classical topology, inclusions that arise from smooth neighborhood deformation retracts behave like cofibrations: they satisfy the smooth homotopy extension property.

So the relationship is:

\[
\text{smooth NDR-pair} \implies \text{smooth cofibration}.
\]

In many well-behaved situations, the two notions are essentially equivalent or at least serve the same purpose in constructing cofiber sequences.

---

## Mapping cones and cofibers in Frölicher spaces

Given a smooth map  
\[
f:X\to Y,
\]
the paper constructs its **mapping cone** \(C_f\) in the category of Frölicher spaces.

Formally, one starts with the cylinder or cone on \(X\), for example

\[
CX = X\times I / X\times\{1\},
\]

and glues it to \(Y\) along \(f\):

\[
C_f = Y \cup_f CX.
\]

Equivalently,

\[
C_f = \bigl(Y \sqcup X\times I\bigr)/\sim
\]

where

\[
(x,0)\sim f(x)
\]

and all points of \(X\times\{1\}\) are collapsed to the cone point.

Because the category of Frölicher spaces has suitable quotient and pushout constructions, this mapping cone can be given a natural Frölicher structure.

When \(i:A\hookrightarrow X\) is a smooth cofibration, the mapping cone \(C_i\) is smoothly homotopy equivalent to the quotient

\[
X/A.
\]

Thus for cofibrations, the cofiber can be modeled by the quotient \(X/A\), just as in classical topology.

---

## Construction of the right Puppe sequence

The main use of smooth cofibrations and smooth NDR-pairs is to construct the **right Puppe sequence** in the Frölicher category.

For a smooth map

\[
f:X\to Y,
\]

one forms the mapping cone \(C_f\), then the suspension \(\Sigma X\), and obtains a sequence

\[
X \xrightarrow{f} Y \longrightarrow C_f \longrightarrow \Sigma X \xrightarrow{\Sigma f} \Sigma Y \longrightarrow \Sigma C_f \longrightarrow \Sigma^2 X \longrightarrow \cdots .
\]

This is the right Puppe sequence.

For a smooth cofibration

\[
i:A\hookrightarrow X,
\]

the sequence takes the familiar cofiber form

\[
A \xrightarrow{i} X \longrightarrow X/A \longrightarrow \Sigma A \xrightarrow{\Sigma i} \Sigma X \longrightarrow \Sigma(X/A) \longrightarrow \Sigma^2 A \longrightarrow \cdots .
\]

The connecting map

\[
X/A \longrightarrow \Sigma A
\]

is obtained by comparing the quotient/cofiber with the mapping cone construction. Smoothness of this connecting map depends on the cofibration/NDR hypotheses.

The paper’s point is that, under the smooth cofibration condition, the usual Puppe-sequence construction works in the Frölicher category: mapping cones, suspensions, quotients, and connecting maps are all legitimate smooth constructions.

---

## Summary

The paper says, in essence:

1. **Smooth cofibrations** are maps satisfying the smooth homotopy extension property.

2. **Smooth neighborhood deformation retracts** give a useful geometric criterion for smooth cofibrations.

3. If \(i:A\hookrightarrow X\) is a smooth cofibration, then the quotient \(X/A\) behaves as the smooth cofiber of \(i\).

4. Using mapping cones and suspensions in the category of Frölicher spaces, one obtains the **right Puppe sequence**
   \[
   A\to X\to X/A\to \Sigma A\to \Sigma X\to \Sigma(X/A)\to\cdots .
   \]

5. The smooth cofibration condition ensures that this construction is homotopically well-behaved in the smooth Frölicher setting, just as cofibrations do in ordinary algebraic topology.

The work studies cofibrations in the category of Frölicher spaces and relates them to smooth homotopy-theoretic constructions. A smooth map \(i:A\hookrightarrow X\) is treated as a cofibration when it satisfies the smooth homotopy extension property: for every Frölicher space \(Y\), smooth homotopy on \(X\) compatible with a given homotopy on \(A\) extends smoothly over \(X\).

A central result characterizes suitable closed inclusions \(A\subset X\) as smooth neighborhood deformation retracts. Namely, under appropriate hypotheses, \(A\) is a cofibrant subspace precisely when there exists a smooth neighborhood \(U\) of \(A\) in \(X\) and a smooth deformation retraction
\[
r_t:U\to U,\qquad r_0=\mathrm{id}_U,\quad r_1(U)\subset A,\quad r_t|_A=\mathrm{id}_A .
\]
This gives a geometric criterion for cofibrations analogous to the classical Strøm/NDR characterization in topology, but formulated in the Frölicher setting.

The paper then applies this characterization to homotopy cofiber constructions. For a cofibration \(A\hookrightarrow X\), the quotient \(X/A\), mapping cone, and suspension behave well in the smooth homotopy category. Consequently one obtains Puppe sequences
\[
A \longrightarrow X \longrightarrow X/A \longrightarrow \Sigma A
   \longrightarrow \Sigma X \longrightarrow \Sigma(X/A)\longrightarrow \cdots,
\]
whose connecting maps are smooth and whose exactness properties mirror the classical topological case. Thus the work provides a smooth Frölicher-space framework in which cofibrations, deformation retracts, cofibers, and Puppe exact sequences are compatible.
